official_measurement_examples.name: 20 cubic metre threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance says taking more than 20 cubic metres of water per day is likely to require an abstraction licence, subject to the detailed exemptions and rules.

official_measurement_examples.name: ALS boundary limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 ALS boundary dataset is a national reference showing areas where technical assessments exist and explicitly is not suitable for detailed technical assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Water availability not guarantee
official_measurement_examples.fact: Catchment licensing strategies can indicate water availability, but Environment Agency guidance states this does not guarantee an application will succeed because local factors and environmental constraints still apply.

official_measurement_examples.name: Supply reliability limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Licences may include hands-off-flow or hands-off-level conditions and a granted licence does not guarantee a continuous supply of water in dry conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Trade hydrological link
official_measurement_examples.fact: April 2026 trading guidance states abstraction-right trades require case-specific assessment and can only take place where there is a hydrological link.

official_measurement_examples.name: Application notice distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A public notice that an abstraction application has been made is consultation evidence and must not be represented as an issued licence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Licence lifecycle
official_measurement_examples.fact: Abstraction and impoundment licences can be varied transferred or revoked and compliance is assessed separately, so historic licence evidence must retain current status and conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Water abstraction or impoundment licensing, planning permission, land rights and water-company supply capacity are separate questions and none alone establishes parcel development capacity.

core_rules: ALS boundary mapping is not site-specific water availability proof
water availability in an ALS does not guarantee a licence
an abstraction licence application is not an issued licence
an issued abstraction licence is not planning permission
planning permission is not an abstraction licence
the 20 cubic metre threshold must retain exemptions and aggregation rules
hands-off-flow and hands-off-level conditions affect reliability and must not be ignored
a licence does not guarantee continuous water supply
water-right trading requires regulatory approval and hydrological linkage
historic licence data must retain variation transfer revocation and expiry context
compliance scoring is distinct from licence existence
catchment strategy colours are not parcel development scores
water-right evidence does not determine land ownership
abstraction rights do not reserve utility or development capacity
no parcel abstraction clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
